documents: Published paper: Rimando, Williamson, Mendoza & Hobbs (2022), Source Model and Characteristics of the 27 July 2022 MW 7.0 Northwestern Luzon Earthquake, Philippines, Seismica 1(1), PDF pp. 1-8

entry.evidence: a distribution which makes it difficult to ascertain the preferred fault plane from seismicity alone

steps.action: The authors take the live 27 July 2022 Mw 7.0 Abra earthquake as the found event, with location and depth from PHIVOLCS.
steps.quote: northwestern region of the island of Luzon, northern Philippines was hit by a moment magnitude (MW) 7.0 earthquake

steps.action: The authors take PHIVOLCS and USGS focal mechanisms and the two-week aftershock distribution from agency reports.
steps.quote: consistently suggest oblique-reverse faulting on either a N-striking, E-dipping or a SW-striking, NW-dipping fault

steps.action: The authors pose the question of which fault plane ruptured, since the aftershocks are ambiguous and no surface rupture has been mapped.
steps.quote: a distribution which makes it difficult to ascertain the preferred fault plane from seismicity alone

steps.action: The authors note PHIVOLCS's proposal that the Abra River Fault is the causative fault.
steps.quote: PHIVOLCS suggests the Abra River Fault (ARF) as a candidate fault for the earthquake rupture

steps.action: The authors processed a descending-track Sentinel-1A pair with GMTSAR: SRTM topographic correction, Gaussian filtering, a coherence mask, SNAPHU unwrapping and GACOS tropospheric correction, giving a LOS displacement map.
steps.quote: We used the descending track (20220721-20220802) Sentinel-1A synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) single-look complex images

steps.action: The authors chose two candidate rupture planes, guided by the focal mechanisms, the LOS pattern and mapped faults: the Vigan-Aggao Fault and a plane parallel to and west of the ARF, both dipping 30°E.
steps.quote: we explored the possibility of rupture along and parallel to two local faults: the Vigan-Aggao Fault (VAF) and the Abra River Fault (ARF)

steps.action: The authors set aside three faults without testing them: the Naglibacan and Bangui faults (sub-optimal orientation) and the ARF itself (documented as strike-slip).
steps.quote: rupture along the ARF itself, which has been suggested by PHIVOLCS to be the likely causative fault (PHIVOLCS, 2022d), is unlikely

steps.action: The authors forward-modelled the USGS teleseismic finite-fault plane to predict LOS displacement at the inversion's data locations, as a rival geometry.
steps.quote: modeled the expected LOS displacement at the same locations as used in our source inversion

steps.action: The authors inverted the LOS data for static slip on each candidate plane with MudPy, using frequency-wavenumber Green's functions in a CRUST1 velocity model, a 0-90° rake window and Tikhonov smoothing.
steps.quote: To invert for the slip, we used the MudPy modeling and source inversion toolkit

steps.action: The authors varied the regularization constant over a range of values and chose solutions near the bend of an L-curve (Fig. S1).
steps.quote: We test our inversion results over a range of values, opting for the model that minimizes the data misfit without overfitting

steps.action: The authors describe the LOS displacement pattern (a positive lobe beneath the northern ARF, a negative lobe to the SSE) and read it, given the focal mechanisms, as dominantly reverse motion.
steps.quote: Results show a lobe of positive LOS deformation beneath the northern ARF, and a lobe of negative LOS deformation to the SSE.

steps.action: The authors report the slip distributions: diffuse deep reverse slip (peak 64 cm) on the VAF and localized reverse slip (peak 95 cm at 13-16 km) on the ARF-parallel plane.
steps.quote: This model exhibits more localized reverse-slip (average 67° rake) at shallower depths and with a higher peak slip value (95 cm)

steps.action: The authors compared the three geometries by overall L2 misfit (Table 1) and by residual maps (Fig. 3 G-I).
steps.quote: Table 1 also includes the overall L2 norm misfit for each model.

steps.action: The authors kept the ARF-parallel plane as the preferred model, because it visually best reproduces the LOS near the rupture, although its L2 misfit is similar to the VAF's.
steps.quote: the modeled rupture on the ARF-parallel fault plane is the preferred model for this study as it visually most closely reproduces

steps.action: The authors derived expectations from the preferred model: possible surface rupture west of Abra and possible stress transfer onto the ARF.
steps.quote: there may well be surface rupture to the west of Abra, near the most productive aftershock region

steps.action: The authors weighed the VAF model, which has the lowest misfit, against published morphotectonic evidence that the VAF is dominantly strike-slip, and found them contradictory.
steps.quote: the dominantly reverse-slip kinematics that our model suggests is contradictory to the dominantly strike-slip displacement that has been documented through detailed mapping

steps.action: The authors rejected the USGS fault plane as causative, because of its highest misfit and its residuals against the southern positive LOS.
steps.quote: We therefore consider this as an unlikely causative fault for this event.

steps.action: The authors read the reverse-slip ARF-parallel rupture as support for complex shear partitioning, with convergence taken up by faults within crustal blocks.
steps.quote: further supports a complex shear partitioning model for the Philippine archipelago

end.claim: The 2022 Mw 7.0 Luzon earthquake most likely ruptured an unmapped, east-dipping, reverse-slip-dominated fault west of and parallel to the Abra River Fault, with peak slip of 95 cm at 13-16 km depth.

decisive_move.sentence: Inverting the Sentinel-1A LOS displacement for slip on the candidate planes is what produced the slip models that the preference among rival faults rests on.

gates.evidence: Action: the InSAR data are routine Sentinel-1A acquisitions; hypotheses guided only the choice of fault planes for modelling, not data acquisition (p. 2-4). Claim: the rival geometries could misfit the data, and the USGS plane did (p. 6). But the VAF and ARF-parallel planes have similar misfits (0.79 vs 0.83), and the preference rests on visual fit and kinematic compatibility (p. 6). Registration: nothing stated as fixed before the data were seen; the candidate planes were chosen partly from 'the visible pattern of line-of-sight deformation' (p. 3).

imports.item: Tikhonov regularization of the ill-posed slip inversion (Tikhonov 1963; Mair 1994)
SNAPHU statistical-cost network phase unwrapping (Chen & Zebker, J. Opt. Soc. Am. A)

novelty_claims.quote: This study presents the first interferometric synthetic-aperture radar (InSAR)-based fault source model for the 2022 MW 7.0 northwestern Luzon earthquake
the fact that a previously unmapped ARF-parallel fault may exist

limits: Composition is none_fits: this is a rapid single-event source inversion that compares three rival geometries by misfit to one InSAR track. There are no repeated independent traces (so not trace_series) and no crucial test separating the two leading rivals (so not strong_inference). The headline claim is best_explanation, chosen partly by visual fit and kinematic plausibility, although the VAF model has the lowest L2 misfit. The slip distribution sub-claim (peak 95 cm at 13-16 km, average rake 67°) is an estimate without stated uncertainty or resolution analysis, so it falls short of estimate_with_resolution; the authors themselves point to Bayesian inversion as future work (p. 7). Only one descending track was available, with no ascending track, GNSS, or field rupture data. Fault dips were fixed at 30° and the optimum plane was not searched ('beyond the scope of this rapid study', p. 4). Three faults (Naglibacan, Bangui, the ARF itself) were set aside without modelling. The acknowledgements mention anonymous reviewers, but no review file was supplied, so changes made in review cannot be coded. Inference: the L-curve figures and per-model details (Figs. S1-S8) are in a supplement that was not supplied.

disagreements.target: PHIVOLCS (2022d) suggestion that the Abra River Fault is the causative fault
disagreements.support: The ARF is documented as dominantly strike-slip (Pinet and Stephan 1990), while the event and the LOS pattern indicate reverse slip, so the authors model a separate plane west of the ARF.
disagreements.quote: rupture along the ARF itself, which has been suggested by PHIVOLCS to be the likely causative fault (PHIVOLCS, 2022d), is unlikely

disagreements.target: USGS (2022) finite fault model and fault plane solution
disagreements.support: A forward model of the USGS slip gives the highest L2 misfit (1.2) and strong residuals against the positive LOS deformation further south.
disagreements.quote: the USGS forward model is associated with the highest overall misfit and strongest residuals

alternatives_considered.reason: Limited size of the earthquake and distribution of deformation

alternatives_considered.chosen: Model the VAF and an ARF-parallel plane west of the ARF

alternatives_considered.reason: Naglibacan and Bangui have sub-optimal orientations relative to the PHIVOLCS focal mechanism; the ARF is documented as dominantly strike-slip

alternatives_considered.chosen: Fixed planar faults with 30°E dip, consistent with the focal mechanisms
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Investigation of the optimum fault plane
alternatives_considered.reason: Beyond the scope of this rapid study

alternatives_considered.chosen: Regularization constant near the bend of the L-curve
alternatives_considered.alternatives: A range of regularization constant values
alternatives_considered.reason: Minimizes data misfit without overfitting or an overly rough solution

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Bayesian inverse modeling with MCMC/Metropolis-Hastings (Bagnardi and Hooper 2018)

alternatives_considered.chosen: ARF-parallel fault plane as preferred model
alternatives_considered.alternatives: VAF plane (lowest L2 misfit); USGS plane
alternatives_considered.reason: Visually closest reproduction of the LOS near the expected rupture; the VAF's reverse kinematics contradict its documented strike-slip; the USGS plane has the highest misfit
